## Survey open-0: LIN-4476 @ 47fb6af60

Read at SD `origin/main` 47fb6af60 (LIN-4474 / PR 1 merged). I didn't read anything after that: not the `feat/lin-4476-session-fold-drivers` branch (f98e442, which is later) and not PR 2's merge in LV. The LV corpus and kit were read at grounding commit e666c4b60.

**The session half is easy. I checked it rather than assuming.** I changed only `stateFor` and `polledItem` in a scratch copy of the `drive` harness (finished→COMPLETED, running→EXECUTING, stopped→CANCELLED, none→no record) and got: `finished` → claimed, `running` → failed (`session-busy`), `stopped` → failed (`was cancelled`), `none` → failed. These match the plan's `sd` cells. One trap: abort, fresh and target rows have no `session` at all. The new "throw on any other value" must apply only to follow-up rows. Otherwise every abort row throws, and the abort branch in `stateFor` still needs its EXECUTING record.

**Where it will be hard: `pinFold` must reproduce a text format that LV defined.** `walkRequestRecords` hasn't changed since 1616b19, and the 8 shared corpus files are byte-identical across repos (I compared the hashes). So any red `fold` row comes from SD rendering records differently from PR 2's renderer, not from fold drift. The two kinds of failure look the same. Concrete hazards:
- A missing `timestamp` gives `at: undefined`, and `JSON.stringify` **drops the key** instead of writing `null`. I checked this. Any inline case without timestamps (cases 1–4 may well have none) fails unless the renderer writes `at ?? null` while keeping `""` as `""`. `model` already falls back to `?? null`, so `""` survives there.
- Projection and field order: only `requestId, model, at` and the five token fields, in LV's order and separators. `agent` and `effort` must be left out.
- Inline `lines` may be objects or strings. The walk expects strings, and its `parseLine` silently drops bad JSON, so a shape mismatch gives zero records rather than an error.

This also shows the ticket is aimed slightly at a symptom. The rendering, meaning the projection plus the format, is a small rule now written twice (LV's kit driver and SD's `pinFold`), and no sha protects it. If PR 2's `fold` area note doesn't specify the text exactly enough to derive from, the honest fix is an LV follow-up that tightens the note. Bending SD's renderer until it matches is the wrong fix.

**Sequencing cost to name in the Lesson.** The header of `test/runner-contract.test.js` only lets SD copy from merged LV main. So once this lands, any SD change that alters `walkRequestRecords` output keeps SD red until LV merges first. That is the intended "one home", but it is cross-repo choreography that a future SD fold fix will hit.

**Smaller points.**
- Write the corpus sha check like `assertFixturePinned`: a function over bytes. The tamper witness can then flip a byte in memory without touching the fixture.
- `docs/areas/stop-hook-and-relay.md` Lessons are 1,506 of 6,144 bytes, so ~250 bytes fits. The Waiting entry to remove is the `request-usage.js` "fold exists twice" one, and it still names `foldTranscriptMessages`.
- The UNPINNED census calls `sdPin` on every row, so the new `fold` case must return a function and never `null`.

**What I'd do first:** before any SD edits, copy the fixture from PR 2's merge into a scratch file. Read the `fold` area note and the LV kit driver's renderer next to each other, and write SD's renderer against the note. Run only the `fold` rows. If they pass, the rest (session mapping, docs, pins) is mechanical. If one fails, you'll know whether to blame the renderer or the cells before the fixture commit is made.

## Survey global: LIN-4476 @ 47fb6af60

Read at SD `47fb6af60` (the LIN-4474 merge). LinearViewer `origin/main` is `302edafc3`, which is PR 2's (#2448) merge commit.

**Where it lands.** `test/runner-contract.test.js` (481 lines). It has one `sdPin` switch, one `pinX` per area, and an unknown-area throw. LIN-4474 cleaned it up: `columnProblems` is gone, and the sha check is now the only drift check. The file is getting better, apart from its header, which grows by one "re-pinned to…" paragraph with every copy. The second place it lands is the transcript corpus, which SD already names three times: `EXPECTED_STAGES` in `transcript-corpus.test.js`, `stageFiles` in `test/helpers/transcript-corpus-walk.js`, and `request-records.json`, which witness (a) pins to `walkRequestRecords`.

**What the obvious way would do.** The plan asks for an id-to-path map of the 8 shared ids. That would be a fourth naming of the corpus layout, and it isn't needed. A fold row's `item.id` is already `<case>/<stage>`, so `stageFiles(path.join(CORPUS, id))` finds the file and `stageSources` reads it. I trial-drove all 14 `fold` rows at base that way (8 corpus, 4 inline, 2 corner). I projected each record as `[requestId, model, at, …TOKEN_FIELDS]` and let JSON render a missing value as `null`. Every `sd` cell matched, and every corpus file's sha256 matched, with no map. `subagent-shared-message` is left out without any special case, because no row names it. If the plan's map is kept, a corpus case added later must be listed by hand, or its row fails with a lookup miss rather than a clear message.

Other checks against PR 2's contract (86 rows):
- **W-4 still holds.** Its row is present and `JSON.stringify(t, null, 2) + "\n"` reproduces the file.
- **`pinReport` can stay unchanged.** The 2 new `report` rows (the http/#x fragment row and the U+2028 row) pass both readings.
- **Session values.** `halt` has 14 rows and uses `finished | none | running | stopped`. The current `stateFor` reads `live` as a finished (`COMPLETED`) session, so the rename fixes a vocabulary bug and isn't only cosmetic. The `running` and `stopped` rows expect `sd: failed`, and `stateFor` has to build those sessions with `followUpTo: ORIG`.

What has to learn about this change:
- The `request-usage.js` Waiting entry has to go.
- The `transcript.js` Waiting entry ("its `report` and `sentinel` rows pin this module's output") and the Lesson that names those rows should mention `fold`. Otherwise the area note under-describes what the copy pins.
- Stop-hook Lessons are at 1,507 of 6,144 bytes, so a 250-byte lesson fits.
- Nothing fails if the module-map line is skipped.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Resolve fold ids through `stageFiles` instead of adding a map, and assert that each id has exactly one file.
- Put the projection in one named function next to `pinFold`, so the tuple order is written down once.
- Trim the header's re-pin history to the current copy. Git keeps the rest.

**Symptom, not cause.** The timestamp wart has a twin: the `corner: model ""` row carries a `difference` for the same reason. `walkRequestRecords` applies `nonEmptyString` to the id but not to `model` (`message.model ?? null`) or `at` (`entry.timestamp`). The follow-up ticket should cover both fields, as one rule for the whole record. Per the new Lesson, the fix re-pins in LinearViewer first, and both `difference` rows go away together.

**Not this task's to carry:** making the fold one piece of shared code. With the pin in place, two copies plus a drift check meets the "one home" rule.

## LIN-4476 · implementation summary (PR 3, SD)

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/341
**Head:** `7ac59a33519bac7aa3f273eb8e2059a2bd27f055` (`feat/lin-4476-merged-contract-session-fold`, four commits on `origin/main` 47fb6af)

**CI:** the repository's `unit tests` check (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `npm ci` + `npm test`, ubuntu-latest, Node 22) completed **SUCCESS** on the head above (run 43540260610, 2m55s). Confirmed on the rollup, not just triggered.

**What it does:** copies the merged contract from LinearViewer `302edafc3` (LIN-4475) byte for byte (66 → 86 rows); maps the session vocabulary (`running`/`finished`/`stopped`/`none`, throwing on `live` and any other follow-up value); adds `pinFold`, pinning the 14 `fold` rows to `walkRequestRecords` against SD's own copies of the 8 shared corpus files; docs (settled Waiting entry removed, one Lesson, module-map line).

**Retires:** SD's unpinned half of W8 (the transcript fold); SD's unpinned half of W5's vocabulary (`live`); the `request-usage.js` fold Waiting entry.

**Leftover:** the SD `timestamp: ""` wart (SD posts `at: ""`; the kit writes `null`) is **not fixed here**. Follow-up: **LIN-4477**, related to LIN-4476.

**Merge:** not done by this task. LIN-4476 is not marked Done.

## Review — LIN-4476

Reviewed SD PR [#341](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/341), head `7ac59a33519bac7aa3f273eb8e2059a2bd27f055` (4 commits on `origin/main` 47fb6af). LV `origin/main` is `302edafc3` (PR 2's squash merge). Nothing in LV's `lib/runner-kit` has changed since.

CI: green. The `unit tests` check (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) passed on head `7ac59a3`, run 43540260610. I also ran it locally on that head: `npm test` gave 4396 tests, 4390 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped.

### Re-grounding and regression
- `git log --since=2026-11-13T20:29:45Z` on the touched files shows only LIN-4474's three commits (0306d4b, 427b36c, 54b1870), and this PR builds on them. `columnProblems` stays retired. The LIN-4385 guard in `pinReport` (both readings checked against `row.sd`, from 9620f44) is untouched. The unknown-area throw in `sdPin` is kept. Nothing reverted is re-applied.
- Fixture bytes: `sha256(test/fixtures/runner-contract.json)` on the head, `302edafc3:lib/runner-kit/contract.json`, and LV `origin/main:lib/runner-kit/contract.json` all equal `871ca615…23a2`. That also equals LV `CONTRACT_SHA256` (`tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js:55`) and SD's `FIXTURE_SHA256`. The copy and the constants landed in one commit (b2f07fe).

### Against what was asked, sentence by sentence
- **Copy the fixture byte for byte from PR 2's merge commit, and update `LV_COMMIT` and `FIXTURE_SHA256` in the same commit.** Met: b2f07fe, sha values above.
- **`stateFor` and `polledItem` map running→EXECUTING, finished→COMPLETED, stopped→CANCELLED, none→absent, and throw on `live` and any other value.** Met by `phaseOfSession`. The guard applies to follow-up rows only, so abort keeps its EXECUTING record (survey open-0 trap avoided).
- **Add `pinFold`: drive `walkRequestRecords` over the `fold` rows and sha-check each corpus file against an 8-id map, excluding `subagent-shared-message`.** Met. `FOLD_CORPUS` has exactly 8 ids. The survey's `stageFiles` alternative was declined, and the PR gives the reason: the ticket asked for the map.
- **Add `case 'fold'` to `sdPin` and keep the unknown-area throw.** Met.
- **Render absent as `null` and keep `""` as `""`.** Met (`renderFold`). The PR says correctly that the absent-timestamp test does not tell `?? null` apart from plain array serialisation. That is harmless.
- **Leave `pinReport` and the `created` layer alone.** Met: neither is in the diff.
- **Remove the `request-usage.js` fold Waiting entry.** Met.
- **Add a Lesson of about 250 bytes, plus the same line in `docs/module-map.md`.** Met (243 bytes). Stop-hook Lessons stay well under 6,144 bytes, and the docs guards pass in CI.
- **Name the `timestamp: ""` wart as a leftover and file a follow-up.** Met: LIN-4477 is filed, related to this issue, and named in the PR's Leftover section. Its description also notes the `model ""` twin, as survey global asked.
- **If `sd` cells mismatch, correct LV, never SD's copy.** Not triggered: all 14 fold rows and every session row pass on the copied fixture without changes.
- **Testing: `pinFold` passes every fold row; session rows pass and the guard throws on `live`; a corpus-byte tamper fails its sha check.** Met, with the gap described under mutation checks (ledger item 1).
- **Testing: SD suite and CI green on the merge commit; close-out cross-repo byte and sha check; re-run `lin-4202-runner-kit-records` in LV.** These come after the merge (ledger 3–4). The byte and sha equality already holds before the merge.
- **Retires: say what it retires in the PR.** Met. The PR names W8's SD half, W5's `live`, and the Waiting entry. The diff removes that Waiting entry.
- **Start from the PR 3 branch PR 2 prepared; where the code shows the plan is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4461.** The course change is right: the prepared branch `f98e442` copies LV's unmerged `4436d443c`, which SD's header forbids, so the PR rebuilt fresh from `origin/main`. But the departure is recorded only in the PR body. **No comment on LIN-4461** says so. Close-out fix 2.

### Mutation checks (each reverted; tree clean afterwards)
- `stopped: PHASES.CANCELLED` changed to `COMPLETED`: the vocabulary message test and `halt: follow-up to a stopped session…` go red. ✔
- `live: PHASES.COMPLETED` added to `SESSION_PHASE`: W-2 goes red. ✔
- `case 'fold'` removed from `sdPin`: all 14 fold rows go red. ✔
- With the sha call present, appending a byte to `mixed-model/final/mixed-session.jsonl` turns the row `fold: corpus mixed-model/final` red. ✔
- **With `assertCorpusPinned(...)` removed from `pinFold`, the suite stays fully green (92 pass, 0 fail).** With the call removed and the on-disk tamper (a trailing newline) applied, the row also stays green. Only the tamper test's precondition goes red, because it reads the real file. So the tamper witness proves the check function but not that `pinFold` calls it. Close-out fix 1.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The change is isolated. Other `'live'` hits in SD (`instance-guard.js`, `reapers.js`, `signal-guard.js`) are process-liveness verdicts, not the contract's session vocabulary. `foldTranscriptMessages` no longer appears anywhere in SD. The `model ""` / `timestamp ""` pair is one rule, and LIN-4477 covers both fields. That ticket is outside this one and already filed.

### Fixes for close-out (make them before merging)
1. **`test/runner-contract.test.js`, the `describe('runner contract table (LIN-4476): the fold pin')` block.** Add a test that drives `pinFold` itself with a wrong sha, so it can't stay green if the call is unwired. For example: `const row = TABLE.rows.find((r) => r.area === 'fold' && r.case === 'corpus mixed-model/final'); assert.throws(() => pinFold({ ...row, item: { ...row.item, sha256: '0'.repeat(64) } }), /the corpus bytes differ/);`. Check that it goes red with the `assertCorpusPinned` line in `pinFold` commented out.
2. **LIN-4461**: post a short comment recording the course change. PR 3 was built fresh from SD `origin/main` 47fb6af, not from the prepared branch `feat/lin-4476-session-fold-drivers` (f98e442), because that branch copies LV's unmerged `4436d443c`. The copy now comes from merge `302edafc3`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **Inside** (testing clause "a corpus-byte tamper fails its sha check"): `pinFold` calling the sha check is not witnessed. Settle before the merge with close-out fix 1. The pass condition: the new test goes red when the call is removed and green when it is restored.
2. **Inside** (the "change course and say so on LIN-4461" clause): the departure is not recorded on the parent. Settle before the merge with close-out fix 2 (the comment exists on LIN-4461).
3. **Inside** (testing: "SD's full suite and CI are green on the merge commit"): CI ran on the PR head, not on the merge commit. Settle after the merge: the `unit tests` check is green on the SD `main` merge commit.
4. **Inside** (close-out cross-repository check): settle after the merge. On fresh fetches, `sha256(LV origin/main:lib/runner-kit/contract.json) == sha256(SD origin/main:test/fixtures/runner-contract.json) == CONTRACT_SHA256 == FIXTURE_SHA256` (currently `871ca615…`). Then re-run `tests/…/lin-4202-runner-kit-records` in LV, and LV's suite, and both must pass. Close LIN-4476, then LIN-4461, only after this passes.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Blind read
Verdict: same. Better: `test/runner-contract.test.js` gives the follow-up session vocabulary one owner (`phaseOfSession`, used by both `stateFor` and `polledItem`) that throws on an unknown value, where any non-`live` value used to fall through to "gone" quietly, and `sdPin` learns the new `fold` area. Worse: `pinFold` adds a second expected copy of `walkRequestRecords` output over the same corpus stages that `test/fixtures/transcript-corpus/request-records.json` already pins, plus a third hand-kept list of corpus stages (`FOLD_CORPUS`), and it pins SD's empty-`at` behaviour that the contract itself says Harbour rejects (`request-usage.js`).

Read: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/341 at `7ac59a335` against `47fb6af60`.

### Inside the area, fix-sized
- `test/runner-contract.test.js` (stop-hook-and-relay): the LIN-4476 re-pin note says the copy is "adding ... the `report` rows", but the `report` area has been there since the LIN-4385 copy (7 rows). This copy only takes it to 9. Fix: say "two more `report` rows" so the next person re-pinning can trust the row arithmetic.
- `test/runner-contract.test.js` (stop-hook-and-relay): `pinFold` reads a corpus file with its own `bytes.toString('utf8').split('\n')`, without trimming, so the walker gets a trailing empty line. It also hands the walker a made-up agent `'a1b2c3d4'`. `test/helpers/request-usage-lines.js` `stageSources`/`stageFiles` already own how a corpus stage turns into walker sources. Fix: keep the sha256 check on the file bytes, but build `lines`/`agent` through `stageSources(path.join(CORPUS_DIR, row.item.id))`, so the corpus has one reader.

### Inside the area, larger
- `request-usage.js` (stop-hook-and-relay): the new `fold` corner rows record that SD posts `model: ""` and copies `at: ""` raw, which Harbour's intake rejects ("at is not a valid time"). The change pins that behaviour: the row's `sd` value, plus the new test "an empty string stays \"\"" in `test/runner-contract.test.js`. It does not fix it. A fix changes the fold output, and `docs/module-map.md` now says changed fold output has to be re-pinned in LinearViewer first. That makes it a cross-repo change and a decision about what SD should post, so it is larger than a fix.
- `test/runner-contract.test.js` / `test/fixtures/transcript-corpus/request-records.json` (stop-hook-and-relay): the expected per-request records for the same 8 corpus stages now live in two places. One is `request-records.json` (witnessed by `test/request-usage-corpus.test.js`). The other is the contract's `fold` rows (rendered by `renderFold`). The stage list now lives in three places: `EXPECTED_STAGES` in `test/transcript-corpus.test.js`, the keys of `request-records.json`, and `FOLD_CORPUS`. A change to the walk or the corpus has to move all of them together. Picking which copy is the reference, and deriving or retiring the others, is a design decision across the contract and the corpus tests, not a fix.

### Outside the area
None.

## Close-out — LIN-4476

**Merged:** SD PR [#341](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/341), merge commit `7d5fe7d9473232152365e6837ececcd6f2876987`, merged with `--match-head-commit aab9273c5c24987699ceddd163c7a8d8ba79e936` after CI passed on that exact head. Review's account stands for how it meets the ask: byte-for-byte contract copy from LV `302edafc3` (86 rows), the guarded session mapping, `pinFold` over all 14 fold rows with the explicit eight-id corpus map, the `fold` case in `sdPin`, and the notes. It retires SD's unpinned half of W8 (the transcript fold), SD's half of W5's vocabulary (`live`), and the `request-usage.js` fold Waiting entry.

**Changes I made after approval** (commit `aab9273c5`, on top of reviewed head `7ac59a335`):
- **Review fix 1:** added `pinFold itself fails a corpus row whose sha256 is wrong…` in `test/runner-contract.test.js`. It calls `pinFold` with a `mixed-model/final` row whose `item.sha256` is zeros and expects `/the corpus bytes differ/`.
- **Blind read, report-row note:** the re-pin header now says "two more `report` rows (9 in all)".
- **Blind read, one corpus reader:** `pinFold` still hashes the file bytes, but builds walker sources with `stageSources(path.join(CORPUS_DIR, row.item.id))`. The hand `split('\n')` and the invented `a1b2c3d4` agent are gone for corpus rows. Inline rows get `agent: 'main'`.
- **Review fix 2:** the course change is posted on LIN-4461 (comment 37acba0b).

**Ledger**
1. *pinFold calls the sha check (inside):* settled by a run. With the `assertCorpusPinned(...)` call commented out in `pinFold`, the new test fails (suite 92 pass, 1 fail). With it restored the suite is green (93 pass, 0 fail).
2. *Course change on LIN-4461 (inside):* settled, comment 37acba0b-c5cf-4541-8f4d-f30ffb6fa5d6.
3. *Suite and CI green on the merge commit (inside):* the SD `unit tests` check on `main` at `7d5fe7d94` finished success (run 43541767030). Before the merge, the head CI run 43541454125 passed on `aab9273`, and the local `npm test` gave 4397 tests, 4391 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped.
4. *Cross-repository check (inside):* on fresh fetches, `sha256(LV origin/main:lib/runner-kit/contract.json)` equals `sha256(SD origin/main:test/fixtures/runner-contract.json)`, both `871ca615f627a02611957489f3abc83498f1dca64af07259800a174148ba23a2`. That also equals LV `CONTRACT_SHA256` and SD `FIXTURE_SHA256`. In LV at `302edafc3`, `lin-4202-runner-kit-records` and `runner-kit-contract` pass (143 tests, 0 fail), and `npm run test:unit` passes (25,969 tests, 0 fail). The Playwright e2e half of LV's `npm test` was not run. It is unrelated to this change, and nothing in LV changed.
- **Blind read, inside the area but larger:** the duplicated expected fold records across `request-records.json` and the contract's `fold` rows, and the three hand-kept corpus stage lists. Both are a design choice across the contract and the corpus tests. I left them undone, because choosing a single reference is a design change and not a fix. It is recorded here and in the Open questions of the brief.
- **Outside:** none from review or the blind read. The `timestamp: ""` / `model: ""` wart is LIN-4477, filed earlier and already related to this ticket. I set its priority to Medium and added the Bug label, each with a reason on the ticket.

**Deploy:** SD's change is tests and docs only, so nothing deploys. No post-deploy step is outstanding.

**Final CI:** green on the merge commit (above).

## Autopilot run summary (stepper) — LIN-4476

**Outcome:** complete and verified. SD PR #341 merged at `7d5fe7d9473232152365e6837ececcd6f2876987`; LIN-4476 is Done.

**Steps run (kind sequence, converging, no repeats):** survey-task → survey-place → scoping ("just the task", no cuts) → implementation in 5 warm beats (root dispatch bd9fbcf4) → review (Approve, conditional; 4-item ledger) → blind-read ("same") → close-out.

**Beats:** 1/5 fixture copy and pins (b2f07fe) · 2/5 session mapping, red-before observed (8ed256e) · 3/5 `pinFold`, tamper test and renderer mutant each seen failing (4371471) · 4/5 docs, 243-byte Lesson, follow-up LIN-4477 (7ac59a3) · 5/5 PR, CI, summary. Each beat was challenged against its recap before the next went out; beat 1's fixture hash was re-derived independently from LinearViewer at 302edafc3.

**Evidence I checked myself (not the workers' reports):**
- PR #341 state MERGED, 4 files touched (the fixture, the contract test, the area note, the module map).
- `unit tests` check on the merge commit 7d5fe7d94: completed / success. SD `main` head equals that commit.
- `sha256` of `test/fixtures/runner-contract.json` (SD main) equals `sha256` of `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` (LV main): `871ca615f627a02611957489f3abc83498f1dca64af07259800a174148ba23a2`. LV main is still 302edafc3.
- Review and close-out comments are on this ticket (review 39f25bfd, blind read 7f3c3e86, close-out 7d3c12ba).

**What holds:** all of the ask is delivered: byte-for-byte copy, the four-value session mapping with the `live` guard, `pinFold` over the 14 fold rows with the 8-id map, the `sdPin` fold case, the Waiting entry removed, the Lesson and module-map line, and LIN-4477 filed and linked. It retires SD's unpinned half of W8 and of W5's vocabulary (`live`) and the fold Waiting entry.

**What is left (named, not hidden):**
- Close-out left two blind-read items undone as design choices, with its reasons on its comment: the duplicated expected fold records (`request-records.json` vs the contract `fold` rows) and the three hand-kept corpus stage lists. Which copy is the reference is a design decision.
- The `timestamp: ""` / `model: ""` wart is LIN-4477 (not fixed here, as the ticket required).
- LV's Playwright e2e half of `npm test` was not run by close-out (nothing in LV changed; unit suite passed).
- The parent LIN-4461 is not closed by this run; this run was scoped to LIN-4476.

**Process notes:** the wake text labelled several later children as "beat 1/5" (the ROOT's prompt name); I matched them by dispatch id and timing, and no beat was lost. My message after the review dispatch mistyped its id once; the correct id is a9be5996-f879-44de-9351-43a90f299cfe.

description:
## As asked

**Parent:** LIN-4461 (Runs & dispatch: cross-repository contract with simple-dispatcher, piece 8 of LIN-4447). **Repository:** JKershaw/simple-dispatcher (SD). **Landing order:** PR 3 of 3. It is blocked by the PR 2 subtask, because it copies the fixture from PR 2's **merge commit**. LIN-4461 is not done until this merges and the final cross-repository check passes.

**Starting point:** LIN-4461's approved plan. Read the `## Implementation Plan` section of LIN-4461's description in full: "PR 3" under "Per repository, per PR", "Why neither main goes red", "How stale `sd` cells are caught", and witness W-5's PR 3 line. Read the approving verdict (comment f912859d) too. Follow that plan. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4461.

## This piece's slice of the approved plan

**Files and approach** (start from the PR 3 branch the PR 2 subtask prepared):

* `test/fixtures/runner-contract.json`: copy it byte for byte from PR 2's merge commit in LinearViewer. In the same commit, update `LV_COMMIT` and `FIXTURE_SHA256` in `test/runner-contract.test.js`.
* `stateFor` and `polledItem` map the four session values: `running → EXECUTING`, `finished → COMPLETED`, `stopped → CANCELLED`, `none → absent`. They throw on `live` and on any other value.
* Add `pinFold`. It drives `walkRequestRecords` (`request-usage.js`) over the `fold` rows and checks each corpus file's SHA-256 against SD's own id-to-path map, which covers the 8 shared ids only. SD's two `subagent-shared-message` files are excluded.
* Add `case 'fold': return () => pinFold(row)` to `sdPin`. Keep the unknown-area throw.
* Render absent as `null` and keep `""` as `""`, matching LV.
